en.headline: CFS recalls Taiwan rice noodles after trace formaldehyde found
en.dek: A Hsin Tung Yang sample bought from an online shop contained 12 parts per million of formaldehyde, the Centre for Food Safety said.
body: The Centre for Food Safety of the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department said on Saturday that a prepackaged rice noodle sample imported from Taiwan was found to contain a trace amount of formaldehyde. The centre advised the public not to eat the affected batch and told traders holding the product to stop using or selling it.

The product is Hsin Tung Yang Rice Noodles, brand Hsin Tung Yang, origin Taiwan, net weight 300 grams, best before 10 April 2029, distributed by B&S Company. A CFS spokesman said the sample was collected from an online vendor under the Food Surveillance Programme and tested at 12 parts per million of formaldehyde.

The centre said it had instructed the distributor to stop sales, take the batch off shelves and start a recall. Members of the public may call the distributor on 3628 7800 during office hours. Follow-up checks found about 450 cartons of the same batch in the distributor's warehouse, which the centre marked and sealed.

The CFS said that, at the level found, normal consumption would not be expected to harm health. Formaldehyde is classified as a Group 1 carcinogen by the International Agency for Research on Cancer when inhaled; the World Health Organization has said ingestion by mouth is not regarded as carcinogenic. Adding formaldehyde as a food preservative is nevertheless prohibited in Hong Kong, with a maximum penalty of a HK$50,000 fine and six months' imprisonment.

The centre said it had stepped up formaldehyde testing at import and retail level, taking more than 70 recent samples of cabbage, other vegetables and rice noodles. Apart from this sample, no other unsatisfactory results had been recorded. Between January 2023 and July 2026 it tested more than 175 rice-noodle samples, all of which passed. The investigation continues.

zh.headline: 台灣新東陽新竹米粉驗出微量甲醛 食安中心召回
zh.dek: 食物安全中心表示，網店抽查的新東陽新竹米粉樣本含百萬分之十二甲醛，已指示分銷商停售及回收受影響批次。
body: 食物環境衞生署食物安全中心星期六表示，一個由台灣進口的預先包裝米粉樣本被檢出微量甲醛。中心呼籲市民不要食用受影響批次，業界若持有相關產品亦應停止使用或出售。
產品名稱為新東陽新竹米粉，品牌新東陽，來源地台灣，淨重300克，此日期前最佳為2029年4月10日，分銷商為B&S Company。中心發言人表示，樣本在食物監測計劃下由一間網上商店抽取，檢測結果含百萬分之十二的甲醛。
中心已知會涉事商戶及分銷商，並指示分銷商即時停售、下架及展開回收。市民可於辦公時間致電分銷商熱線3628 7800查詢回收。追查發現分銷商倉庫存有約450箱同批次產品，中心已即時封存。
中心指，按該樣本驗出的含量，正常食用不會對健康造成不良影響。國際癌症研究機構將甲醛列為第1類致癌物，但僅限於吸入途徑；世界衞生組織近期資料指經口服攝入並不會致癌。然而香港法例禁止將甲醛添加於食物作防腐用途，違例最高可被判罰款5萬港元及監禁3個月。
中心已在進口及零售層面加強甲醛測試，近期抽取超70個白菜、蔬菜及米粉樣本，除本次米粉樣本外暫無其他不合格結果。2023年1月至2026年7月，中心共抽取逾175個米粉樣本作各項檢測，全部通過。追查仍在進行。
